_comment: GPT-6.2 arm at reasoning_effort low for Day-to-Day Bench task set v1 (rooms-os-hub #2051): gpt-6.2-astra and gpt-6.2-sol, released 17 November 2026, scored against gpt-6-astra and gpt-6.1-sol under the same conditions (the main seven-model run used low). Same tasks, graders, output limits (4,096 tokens, reasoning included), judges and repeats as run-config.json. Model entries are copied from gpt-6-astra and gpt-6.1-sol with only model_id, reasoning_effort and the price receipt changed. Prices read on the OpenAI pricing page on 17 November 2026, standard tier, short context: gpt-6.2-astra 8 / 0.40 cached / 40 USD per million tokens, gpt-6.2-sol 2 / 0.10 / 10. The model pages say the API rejects reasoning effort none for both, so low is the lowest effort used. caps_usd are the provider ledgers' lifetime ceilings, unchanged from the OpenAI arms. Results are a separate, labelled run.
approved_by: Kol (repo owner): typed go for the paid runs in the AI Resource Hub session on 15 November 2026, caps 90 USD OpenAI and 60 USD Anthropic; on 17 November 2026, relayed by the Chief of Staff: 'we need to use all those up, as we were using them for benchmarking' (prepaid credit only). OpenAI balance read on the billing page 17 November 2026: 115.58 USD, expiring 20 November 2026, auto-reload off

canary._comment: Second canary, 15 November 2026. The first (run 2026-11-15T031058Z-aa0ee142) took the default two tasks, both short and script-graded, so it proved the transport and the charges and nothing else. These two exercise what it missed: f5-pub-03 has five judged checks and a long prompt, f7-pub-05 is graded by tests in the sandbox.

_judge_candidates_comment: The qualify stage tries every candidate against the frozen samples, cheapest first, and names the panel: on each side the cheapest candidate that passed. Then set judges to that panel. A judge verdict is a small JSON object, so every judge and candidate has an output limit of 400 tokens.
